newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips on dollar covering, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips on dollar covering, seen rangebound.

text.p: * Ringgit fell back on short-covering of dollar positions
* Market awaits Malaysia's trade data for April
The ringgit slipped against the dollar in early Asian trading on short-covering of dollar positions, dealers said.
"Some banks in Singapore are buying back the dollar but volume is not big," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5125/35 a dollar against its opening around 2.5100. It closed at 2.5115/25 in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
Dealers said they expected more dollar covering activities through the day after a heavy sell-off on Wednesday.

Offshore players sold their dollar/ringgit positions on rumours that Bank Negara will adopt the same sort of foreign exchange controls administered in Thailand. The talk started when the central bank called for a meeting on Friday with chief executive officers of some banks.
Banking sources, however, said Bank Negara will be meeting the bankers to discuss routine foreign exchange activities.
Dealers said the ringgit is seen trading between 2.5100 and 2.5150 a dollar, with immediate support for the dollar pegged at 2.5050.
The market was also awaiting the release of Malaysia's trade data for April which was widely expected to be in deficit, dealers said.
There has been speculation that the deficit would be as high as two billion ringgit. Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
